question: What is the biological definition of a tissue?

options.A: A group of similar cells working together for a specific job
options.B: A collection of entirely different organs inside a body cavity
options.C: A single specialized cell performing multiple complex tasks alone
options.D: A fluid medium transporting nutrients throughout the circulatory system

explanation: Tissues are formed when cells with similar structures unite to perform a shared function. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T8#GNS111_U1_T8_h1)

question: Body membranes are primarily composed of which structural elements?

options.A: Rigid mineralized columns supporting the main skeletal frame
options.B: Dense hollow tubes transporting fluid away from the heart
options.C: Thin sheets of tissue covering surfaces and lining cavities
options.D: Isolated floating cells without any fixed structural attachment

explanation: Membranes act as protective or secretory barriers made of tissue sheets across body cavities. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T8#GNS111_U1_T8_h1)

question: Which primary tissue type is responsible for body movement?
explanation: Contractile cells within muscle tissue enable both voluntary movement and involuntary organ functions. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T8#GNS111_U1_T8_h2)

question: Epithelial tissue is primarily found doing what in the body?

options.A: Storing excess fat reserves beneath the deep dermis
options.B: Binding skeletal bones tightly together at movable joints
options.C: Transmitting fast electrical impulses down the spinal cord
options.D: Lining body cavities and covering external surfaces

explanation: Epithelia form protective boundary layers on external skin and internal tract surfaces. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T8#GNS111_U1_T8_h2)

question: Which membrane type lines closed internal cavities like the thorax?
explanation: Serous membranes line closed body cavities and secrete watery fluid to reduce friction. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T8#GNS111_U1_T8_h3)

question: Why are synovial membranes classified differently from mucous or serous membranes?

options.A: They open directly to the external environment via hollow tracts
options.B: They cover the entire outer cutaneous surface of the human body
options.C: They lack any lubricating fluid secretion within the joint cavity
options.D: They are composed entirely of connective tissue without any epithelium

explanation: Synovial membranes contain only connective tissue elements unlike epithelial-based membranes. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T8#GNS111_U1_T8_h3)

question: What is the primary difference between regeneration and fibrosis?

options.A: Fibrosis occurs only in skin, while regeneration occurs in bone
options.B: Regeneration requires surgical intervention, while fibrosis heals naturally
options.C: Regeneration restores normal function, while fibrosis creates scar tissue
options.D: Fibrosis replaces cells perfectly, while regeneration leaves fibrous scars

explanation: Regeneration replaces lost cells with identical functional tissue, whereas fibrosis lays down fibrous scar matrix. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T8#GNS111_U1_T8_h4)

question: Why does damage to cardiac muscle tissue often lead to permanent functional deficits?

options.A: Heart muscle cells divide constantly and overwhelm local blood supply
options.B: Fibrous scar tissue prevents blood from flowing through coronary arteries
options.C: Cardiac tissue lacks any connective tissue elements to form scars
options.D: Cardiac muscle has very poor regenerative capacity and heals via fibrosis

explanation: Adult cardiac muscle cells do not divide readily, so healing produces non-contractile scar tissue. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T8#GNS111_U1_T8_h4)

question: A patient develops a pressure ulcer over the sacrum. Which primary tissue layer is initially compromised?
explanation: Pressure ulcers damage the skin, which is the body's primary cutaneous membrane. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T8#GNS111_U1_T8_h5)

question: Why is adequate nutritional intake essential for a patient with an open surgical wound?

options.A: Vitamins directly destroy bacteria colonizing the deep subcutaneous tissue
options.B: Calories prevent the accumulation of synovial fluid inside joint spaces
options.C: Proteins convert fibrous scar tissue back into functional muscle cells
options.D: Nutrients provide essential building blocks for cellular regeneration and tissue repair

explanation: Cellular proliferation and collagen synthesis during tissue healing require adequate amino acids and vitamins. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T8#GNS111_U1_T8_h5)
